title: Flight booking domain model
idea: The flight domain model splits the physical plane (Aircraft, Seat) from what is sold (Flight, FareClass) and from who bought it (Booking, Passenger, Ticket).

analogy.text: A concert hall, its ticket price tiers, and the guest list. The hall has fixed chairs; tiers sell a number of places; the list names each guest.
analogy.breaks: A Booking can expire on its own; a guest list cannot.

points: An Aircraft owns its Seats; each Seat sits in one Cabin.
A Flight flies one Aircraft on one route and sells several FareClasses.
A Booking buys one FareClass for 1 to 9 Passengers under one PNR.
A Ticket is issued per Passenger and may carry a seat number.

edges.label: flies 1
edges.caption: A Flight is one departure of one Aircraft. Many flights reuse the same aircraft.

edges.label: has 1..*
edges.caption: The Aircraft fixes the seat layout. Each Seat belongs to one Cabin, economy or business.

edges.label: sells 1..*
edges.caption: A Flight sells FareClasses. Each has a cabin, a price in minor units and refund rules.

edges.label: buys 1
edges.caption: A Booking buys one FareClass on one Flight. Its PNR is the reference the traveller sees.

edges.label: has 1..9
edges.caption: A Booking carries one to nine Passengers. The total is price times passenger count.

edges.label: issues 0..*
edges.caption: After payment each Passenger gets a Ticket. A seat number is optional on it.

edges.label: has
edges.caption: BookingStatus is an enum. The state machine page adds the allowed moves.

code.title: The model in Java 17
code.caption: Records for fixed data, a class for Booking because its status and tickets change. Invariants live in constructors.

walk.text: Build an Aircraft with two business and two economy seats.
Two fare classes, prices in paise, and one Flight that sells both.
A two-passenger Booking; its total is price times passengers, status HELD.
Issue a ticket with economy seat 12A for the first passenger; status checks come on page 4.
Three bad inputs: a business seat on an economy fare, a loop route, no passengers.
The Flight constructor refuses a route that starts and ends in one place.
A ticket needs a passenger on this booking and a seat in the fare's cabin.

pitfalls: Do not store booked state on Seat; the same Aircraft flies many Flights.
Keep FareClass separate from Cabin; one cabin sells many fares at different prices.
Never use double for fares; keep money as long minor units.

quiz.q: What does the line after the TK-1 ticket print?
options: rejected: Ravi Rao is not on PNR-1
quiz.why: Seat 1A exists and Ravi is on PNR-1, but 1A is a BUSINESS seat. The Y-SAVER fare is ECONOMY, so the cabin check throws.

takeaway: Plane, product and purchase are different classes; never mix their state.

starters: Why is FareClass not just an enum of cabins?
Where does the per-flight seat map live if not on Seat?
How would a connecting trip with two flights change this model?
